Messages.Author: Jon Stahler
Messages.Body:
On the White Wolf site, the interpretation is that the reduction of blood is
what triggers the burning of the vampire, and hence the pool gain for the
opposing methusalah. How am I to interpret this? We're having a debate in
our playgroup right now concerning the nature of this card. Example:

Vampire A has been named for an Anathema vote. Vampire A enters combat with
Vampire B. Vampire A has one blood on it. Vampire A uses a skin of steel
to prevent the opposing minions strike(s). Does paying for the card
constitute a reduction of blood, and hence cause the vampire to burn? The
site says regardless of the source, which leads me to believe this is the
case. Any clarification would be more than welcome. I'm thinking the
Brujah/Nosferatu princes would be hellacious if this were the case. Thanks
in advance!

Jon

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
>===== Original Message From "Jon Stahler" <sta...@staff.uiuc.edu> =====

>On the White Wolf site, the interpretation is that the reduction of blood is
>what triggers the burning of the vampire, and hence the pool gain for the
>opposing methusalah. How am I to interpret this?

If the vampire's blood level is reduced (from some positive amount) to
zero in combat, the card's effects are applied.

> We're having a debate in
>our playgroup right now concerning the nature of this card. Example:
>
>Vampire A has been named for an Anathema vote. Vampire A enters combat with
>Vampire B. Vampire A has one blood on it. Vampire A uses a skin of steel
>to prevent the opposing minions strike(s). Does paying for the card
>constitute a reduction of blood, and hence cause the vampire to burn?

Yes. He had 1 now he has 0, so there's been a 1-blood-point reduction.
